name: Oberrealta Chapel
key_features: Tiny concrete chapel shaped like a child's drawing of a house, alone on an alpine meadow.

name: Oita Prefectural Library (Art Plaza)
key_features: Hollow precast concrete beams project from the facade as tubes, expressing structure and services.

name: San Miguel Corporation Building
key_features: Office block wrapped in stepped planted terraces and deep sunshades, a tropical take on the tower.

name: Skopje Telecommunications Centre
key_features: Rhythmic concrete towers with flared crowns above a long podium of postal and service halls.

name: Soulages Museum
key_features: Row of Corten steel boxes cantilevered from a slope, with gallery light through glazed ends.

name: Surgical Clinic and Health Centre
key_features: Compressed earth brick wards under a floating double roof, with coloured windows and shaded courts.

name: Swiss National Park Visitor Centre
key_features: Two interlocking white concrete cubes with identical windows and a looping stair between them.

name: The Museum Hotel Antakya
key_features: Hotel raised on a steel deck above excavated Roman mosaics, with rooms as prefabricated modules.

name: Tossols-Basil Athletics Track
key_features: Running track threaded through an oak wood, with trees left standing inside the field.

name: Tulou Collective Housing
key_features: A ring of low-cost rental units around a court reinterprets the Hakka earthen roundhouse.

name: Umbrella House (Kasa no Ie)
key_features: Small square house under a timber umbrella roof of rafters radiating from the centre.

name: Villa Verde Housing
key_features: Timber-framed gabled half-houses, one half built and the other left under the roof for owners to finish.

name: wNw Bar
key_features: Bamboo arches form a dome with a top opening; air cooled over the surrounding lake flows through.

name: Kumano Kodo Nakahechi Museum of Art
key_features: A thin-roofed single-storey box wrapped in layers of clear and milky glass.

name: Hoenheim-Nord Tram Terminus
key_features: Tilted concrete canopy and car park whose white lines and light strips follow the movement of cars and trams.

name: Rue des Suisses Housing
key_features: Street fronts behind folding metal shutters; in the garden, low blocks wrapped in rolling wooden blinds.

name: Villa dall'Ava
key_features: Two boxes on thin, randomly tilted columns, with a rooftop pool aimed at the Eiffel Tower.

name: Pavillon Noir
key_features: A dance centre in a glass box held by a black concrete exoskeleton of slanting struts.

name: Le Volcan
key_features: A white truncated cone and a smaller one rise from a sunken public square.

name: Upper Lawn Pavilion
key_features: Weekend house: a timber and glass box set on and inside the old stone walls of a farm cottage.

name: Hopkins House
key_features: Two-storey steel-frame and glass box, entered by a bridge from the street at upper level; open plan inside.

name: Haus Gugalun
key_features: Old log farmhouse extended into the slope with new timber rooms under one continuous gable roof.

name: Fondazione Giangiacomo Feltrinelli
key_features: A long, thin glass-and-concrete gabled building whose steep roof repeats the rhythm of its frame.

name: Museum of Byzantine Culture
key_features: Brick-faced volumes and deep slots of light lead visitors on a slow route through the collection.

name: Weekend House, Anavyssos
key_features: Thick local-stone piers carry a flat concrete slab, making a shaded portico that wraps two sides of a small house.

name: Silver Hut
key_features: Ito's own house: a courtyard under a field of thin steel-frame vaults, light enough to feel like a tent.

name: SunnyHills at Minami-Aoyama
key_features: A cake shop wrapped in a cloud of interlocking timber strips (jigoku-gumi joinery) that filters the light.

name: Stone Museum (Stone Plaza)
key_features: Old rice stores linked by new walls of thin local Ashino stone louvres and stone screens with gaps for light.

name: Gifu Kitagata Apartment
key_features: A one-room-thick housing slab whose facade grid is punched with double-height open terraces.

name: Garden & House
key_features: A 4 m wide stack of bare concrete slabs with no outside walls: plants, clear railings and curtains make the facade.

name: Roof House
key_features: The gently sloping roof is the living room: a deck for meals, cooking and showers, reached by ladders.

name: Jaú Bus Station
key_features: Bus station under one concrete roof carried on columns that branch out round skylights; ramps link the levels.

name: Forma Furniture Showroom
key_features: A closed prism lifted on two 30 m beams over street parking; one full-width shop window faces the avenue.

name: Maraya
key_features: A concert hall wrapped in 9,740 m2 of mirror, a box that reflects the desert canyon until it nearly disappears.

name: Federation of Industries Building
key_features: One of Chadirji's brick office buildings, his search for a modern architecture rooted in Iraq.

name: Izvestia Building
key_features: Constructivist newspaper office: a grid of big windows topped by a row of round ones.

name: Sarpi Border Checkpoint
key_features: White tower of cantilevered viewing terraces marking the Georgia-Turkey border by the Black Sea.

name: Hotel Kazakhstan
by: Yuri Ratushny, Leonid Ukhobotov, Vladimir Kim
key_features: Tall slab hotel with a crown-like top, built to stand up to Almaty's earthquakes.

name: Flying Saucer (UkrINTEI)
key_features: Saucer-shaped hall hovering over a long low glazed base on a narrow street site.

name: Salyut Hotel
key_features: Round hotel whose floors hang around a concrete core; its planned height was cut by more than half.

name: Zvartnots Airport Old Terminal
by: Artur Tarkhanyan, Spartak Khachikyan, Levon Cherkezyan, Zhorzh Shekhlyan
key_features: Round terminal ringed by gates, with the control tower rising from the centre of the circle.

name: Queen Tamar Airport
key_features: Tiny mountain terminal: a white sculptural tower of cut-out shapes beside a small hall.

name: Central Research Institute of Robotics and Technical Cybernetics
key_features: Concrete research tower shaped like a rocket on its launch pad, built to test space robotics.

name: Fondation Jérôme Seydoux-Pathé
key_features: A curved shell of perforated aluminium rising in a courtyard behind a facade carved by Rodin.

name: Museo Enzo Ferrari
key_features: A yellow aluminium roof, shaped like a car bonnet with air-intake slots, curls round Enzo Ferrari's birthplace.

name: Tbilisi Public Service Hall
key_features: Giant white petal-like roofs on stems shelter a cluster of glass office blocks by the river.

name: Hotel Uzbekistan
key_features: Curved slab whose whole face is a lattice of concrete sun-screens in an eastern pattern.

name: Hassan II Bridge
key_features: Three parallel decks, two for road and one for tram, each carried on low concrete arches across the Bou Regreg.

name: Madinat al-Zahra Museum
key_features: Museum set low into the ground like an excavation: a sequence of courtyards walled in pale concrete.

name: Central Market, Koudougou
key_features: Market of compressed earth blocks built as vaults, domes and arches, with a covered hall of 624 stalls.

name: Jahad Metro Plaza
key_features: Metro entrance rebuilt as linked brick arches and vaults, about 300,000 handmade bricks, around a pedestrian plaza.

name: Entrepreneurship Development Institute of India
key_features: Brick campus of seven or eight blocks along two axes around courtyards, with deep arcades for the heat.

name: Sainsbury Wing, National Gallery
key_features: Portland stone front borrows the old gallery's pilasters, then thins them out; top-lit galleries recall Soane.

name: The Box (Conjunctive Points)
key_features: A skewed box-shaped room perches on an old warehouse roof: part of Moss's remaking of the Hayden Tract.

name: Santa Maria Church, Marco de Canaveses
key_features: A tall white box: two towers frame a 10 m door, and a long low window lets the nave look out at sitting height.

name: Palais des Expositions (Grand Palais), Charleroi
by: AgwA, architecten jan de vylder inge vinck
key_features: 1950s exhibition halls kept and opened up: facades taken off so the central hall becomes a covered public foyer.

name: Stadthaus Scharnhauser Park
key_features: Town hall whose upper floors overhang the square as a deep canopy, with a field of light rods in front.

name: NAVEZ, 5 social housing units
key_features: Five social flats for large families in a slim corner block at the northern entrance to Brussels.

name: Zénith de Strasbourg
key_features: Concert hall wrapped in orange textile membrane over elliptical steel rings that twist as they rise.

name: Katyń Museum
key_features: Museum in a 19th-century citadel fort; a narrow stair cuts straight through the earth rampart.

name: Netherlands Institute for Sound and Vision
key_features: Cube of coloured glass printed with TV images in relief; half the building, the archive, is sunk below ground.

name: Groot Klimmendaal Rehabilitation Centre
key_features: Rehabilitation centre in woodland: long dark volumes stacked and cantilevered over the slope, full of daylight.

name: PLATO Contemporary Art Gallery
key_features: Old municipal slaughterhouse turned art gallery; new concrete panels fill and open its old door and window holes.

name: Hedge House
key_features: Concrete and glass art pavilion in the garden of Kasteel Wijlre, set low between tall hedges.

name: Goldsmith Street
key_features: Passivhaus council homes in tight brick terraces, with a shared planted alley between the back gardens.

name: New Library, Magdalene College
key_features: Brick walls and tall chimneys frame timber reading bays lit from pitched glazed roof lanterns.

name: Stormen Concert Hall and Library
key_features: Concert hall with three venues and a library as a pair; the library's reading room looks out to the harbour.

name: Weald and Downland Gridshell
key_features: Three-domed lattice of thin green oak laths, shaped like a peanut shell, over a sunken artefact store.

name: Krushi Bhawan
key_features: Government office wrapped in a brick screen patterned after Odisha ikat, in three local clays, around public gardens.

name: Sonneveld House
key_features: Nieuwe Bouwen villa of steel and glass, kept with its original interior as a museum house.

name: Schocken Department Store, Chemnitz
key_features: Arched street front of horizontal window strips; now the State Museum of Archaeology (smac).

name: Hotel Avion
key_features: Hotel on a medieval plot about 8 m wide: galleried café floors at shifting levels behind a glazed front.

name: Villa Stiassni
key_features: Functionalist villa for textile industrialist Alfred Stiassni, set in a large terraced garden above Brno.

name: Sanatorium Joseph Lemaire
key_features: Modernist tuberculosis sanatorium by Maxime Brunfaut at Overijse, near Brussels.

name: Vienna Werkbund Estate
by: Josef Frank (plan) with about 30 architects incl. Loos, Rietveld, Neutra, Hoffmann
key_features: Model estate of 70 small houses by about 30 architects, among them Loos, Rietveld, Neutra and Hoffmann.

name: First Christian Church
key_features: Limestone-and-brick church with a 166 ft freestanding tower; among the first modernist churches in the US.

name: Villa Stein-de Monzie (Les Terrasses)
key_features: White box of strip windows set out with regulating lines; a canopy marks the door and a balcony the service entrance.

name: Oca, Ibirapuera Park
key_features: Low white concrete dome pierced by round windows, with curving ramps and floors inside.

name: Brasília Bus Station (Rodoviária do Plano Piloto)
key_features: Multi-level concrete platform at the crossing of Brasília's two axes: buses below, roads over the top.

name: Palácio da Justiça (Ministry of Justice), Brasília
key_features: Glass box behind a row of concrete arches, with water pouring from chutes between them into a pool.

name: Villa Planchart (Quinta El Cerrito)
key_features: Ponti's 'butterfly' villa on a hill over Caracas, with thin floating roofs and walls treated as sheets.

name: Quartier Schützenstraße
key_features: One city block split into many narrow, brightly coloured facades around inner courtyards.

name: Pierresvives
key_features: Long horizontal 'tree trunk' of concrete and glass holding the archives, library and sports offices.

name: Tanzbrunnen (Star Wave Tent)
key_features: Star-shaped fabric membrane pulled up on masts, floating over a dance floor in a fountain basin.

name: Nara Centennial Hall
key_features: Long hall with curved, dark-tiled walls like a ship's hull, beside Nara station.

name: West Village (Basis Yard)
key_features: Five-storey building ringing a whole city block around sports pitches, with a ramp up to the roof.

name: The Circle, Zurich Airport
key_features: A small city of glass-walled blocks and lanes curving along the hill beside the airport terminal.

name: Emerson College Los Angeles
key_features: Ten-storey frame of two slim residential slabs and a bridge, wrapping a sculpted block of classrooms.

name: Kingsgate Bridge
key_features: Concrete footbridge on V-shaped legs, built as two halves along the banks and swung 90° to meet; Grade I.

name: Media-TIC
key_features: Steel-framed cube wrapped in inflatable ETFE cushions that shade the offices from the sun.

name: LocHal
by: Civic Architects, Braaksma & Roos, Inside Outside (Petra Blaisse)
key_features: 1932 locomotive shed turned public library; huge movable textile screens divide the vast hall.

name: Unilever-Haus
key_features: Offices around a tall open atrium, wrapped in a loose ETFE foil skin against the harbour wind.

name: Max Aicher Arena
key_features: Hall about 200 m by 90 m with no inner columns, roofing over the old outdoor speed-skating oval.

name: Museum of Memory and Tolerance
key_features: Seven-level concrete and steel museum facing the Alameda, wrapped round an atrium with a floating Children's Memorial.

name: Sara Kulturhus
key_features: Culture centre and 20-storey hotel tower built in timber; the hotel is stacked prefabricated CLT room modules.

name: Temple Street Parking Garage
key_features: Long concrete car park for 1,280 cars on arched double columns, bridging George Street, with shops below.

name: Institute of Hygiene and Microbiology
key_features: Sculptural concrete research and teaching building, listed as a key work of organic and brutalist post-war modernism.

name: Goce Delčev Student Dormitory
key_features: Exposed-concrete student towers with projecting service shafts and sky bridges, built in two phases.

name: TASS Building
key_features: News-agency headquarters with deep, round-cornered window frames in sandstone and a globe over the entrance.

name: Slovak National Gallery Extension
by: Vladimír Dedeček; renovation by Architekti BKPŠ
key_features: Long gallery wing lifted on piers like a bridge (the 'Overbridge') in front of the older gallery buildings.

name: Kirishima International Concert Hall (Miyama Conseru)
key_features: Shoebox hall bent into a leaf-shaped plan with a keel-like section for sound, set in open hill country.

name: Shanghai Suhe MixC World
key_features: Shopping centre under a park on Suzhou Creek: planted slopes step down into an "urban valley" to the shops.

name: Lanserhof Sylt
key_features: Health resort under Europe's largest thatched roof; ridge and eaves swing with the dunes, loggias cut into the thatch.

name: Kadokawa Culture Museum
key_features: Angular polyhedron clad in 20,000 granite plates, as if rock had broken up through the ground; 8 m bookshelf theatre.

name: National Museum of Japanese History
key_features: Long, low national history museum on the former grounds of Sakura Castle, where the old moat survives.

name: Embassy of Kuwait, Tokyo
key_features: Block-like concrete volumes stacked asymmetrically round a raised courtyard: chancery below, residence above.

name: Komazawa Olympic Park Control Tower and Gymnasium
key_features: A 50 m concrete tower of stacked slab tiers, a modern pagoda, rising from a raised plaza beside the gymnasium.

name: Mt. Fuji World Heritage Centre, Shizuoka
key_features: Inverted cone of hinoki timber lattice over a pool, whose reflection completes the shape of Mount Fuji.

name: The Prince Kyoto Takaragaike (Kyoto Takaragaike Prince Hotel)
key_features: Ring-shaped hotel: 310 rooms along one corridor round a garden court, the rounded tiers stepping back.

name: Helsingborg Concert Hall
key_features: Classic Swedish functionalism: a tall white hall box fronted by a low curved foyer wing.

name: St. Henry's Ecumenical Art Chapel
key_features: Copper-clad, boat-shaped chapel on a rocky ridge, with a pine-ribbed interior like an upturned hull.

name: Gothenburg Law Courts Extension
key_features: A restrained new wing beside the old courthouse, around a top-lit, timber-lined atrium of stairs and galleries.

name: Powerhouse Brattørkaia
key_features: Energy-positive office: a dark wedge whose steep roof is one big solar array, cut by an oval courtyard.

name: The Twist
key_features: Gallery, bridge and sculpture in one: an aluminium-clad box that turns 90° as it spans 60 m over the river.

name: Kela Main Office (National Pensions Institute)
key_features: Red-brick and copper office block stepped round a raised courtyard, with a top-lit main hall inside.

name: Fragrant Hill Hotel
key_features: White walls with grey trim and diamond-patterned openings that frame garden views, after Suzhou houses.

name: National Palace Museum
key_features: Palace-style museum set against a hill: green-tiled roofs, yellow walls and white stairs on a long axis.

name: Ordos Museum
key_features: Rounded, edgeless shell wrapped in polished metal louvres, its form drawn from the Gobi Desert.

name: Ningbo Museum of Art
key_features: Long grey-brick plinth carrying a timber-slatted steel box, reached by bridges across a moat.

name: Forbidden City
key_features: Walled and moated palace city of 980 buildings strung along Beijing's north-south axis.

name: Tour Total (Jean-Monnet-Tower)
key_features: 69 m office tower wrapped in a load-bearing grid of faceted precast-concrete elements that shade its glass.

name: Museum der bildenden Künste, Leipzig
by: Hufnagel Pütz Rafaelian (Karl Hufnagel, Peter Pütz, Michael Rafaelian)
key_features: Glass-clad box on a former city square, framed by lower corner buildings that rebuild the old street block.

name: Kant-Dreieck
key_features: 11-storey tower, a steel cube on a stone base, crowned by a huge sheet-metal 'sail' that turns in the wind.

name: Norddeutsche Landesbank (NORD/LB) Headquarters
key_features: Glass perimeter block around a planted court, with a tower of glass boxes stacked and twisted off a central core.

name: Zentralsparkasse Branch, Favoritenstrasse
key_features: Bank front of bulging, rippling steel panels between plain houses; inside, a giant concrete hand holds the stair.

name: Loisium Wine World
key_features: Aluminium-clad cube sliced by window cuts that trace the old wine cellar tunnels, which visitors walk into.

name: LifeCycle Tower One (LCT ONE)
key_features: Eight-storey timber high-rise prototype: prefab timber-concrete floors round a concrete core, raised in eight days.

name: Frauenmuseum Hittisau
key_features: A plain timber-clad village box with one big glazed front, holding a women's museum above the local fire station.

name: Joan Miró's Studio (Taller Sert)
key_features: Painter's studio under a row of wave-shaped concrete vaults that bring daylight deep into the workspace.

name: Museum of Memory of Andalusia (MA)
key_features: Long white podium cut by an elliptical courtyard whose ramps spiral between the floors.
